passage: When an organization adopts a new software platform or workflow, leaders often measure success by counting how many employees log in during the first month. Yet high initial login rates frequently mask shallow adoption, where people click around briefly before reverting to familiar spreadsheets and manual workarounds. True technological integration requires redesigning daily routines so that the new tool becomes the easiest, most reliable path to completing core tasks. Without hands-on peer coaching, clear transition milestones, and explicit permission to phase out legacy habits, even powerful digital tools end up as expensive shelfware. Sustainable change happens not when technology is merely installed, but when people's habits and incentives align with the new way of working.
